use_case_summary: Core workload: low-latency chat personalization + reranking for ad selection. Target p50 40-60ms, p95 <200ms, p99 <400ms for non-streaming short prompts (<=64 tokens). Streaming chat expected p95 <300ms end-to-end (client-observed). High concurrency: 1.2k QPS peak across region; burst up to 3k QPS for 90s windows. Cost-sensitive; want reserved pool to guarantee tail latency and predictable unit economics.

notes: POC focus: latency alignment + predictability under 99th percentile. They called out production incidents where p99 spikes correlate with prefix cache miss and TLS handshake variance.

Measurement disagreement details: VTC wants SLO measured as client-observed delta from user action -> final payload arrival (includes network, LB, TLS). Redwood's telemetry natively captures server-side generation time (ingress recv to last token send). SE note: need both views and a binding spec.

Streaming vs non-streaming: customer insists on separate SLO buckets. For streaming chat they expect p95 for first-token <120ms and p95 for session-final flush <300ms. Redwood suggested measuring first-byte and final-flush separately and also report chunk latency distribution.

Suggested alignment: define canonical measurement for SLA as 'client-observed first-byte and final-flush using our probe harness' with mutually agreed probe placement (client region egress + VPC egress). Redwood proposes to run side-by-side probes and compare to their production telemetry to establish offset corrections.

SE technical plan: run 100k synthetic requests (mix: 70% short chat <=64 tokens, 20% rerank micro-requests, 10% longer completions) across 3 model variants (base fp16, 8-bit quant, distilled) capturing p50/p95/p99 for both streaming and non-streaming, plus server-side token gen histogram, ingress-to-response, and end-to-end client timings.

Reserved GPU planning note: initial proposal 24 gpus reserved (dedicated pool) to meet their 1.2k QPS baseline w/ target concurrency 40 requests/GPU for short prompts; burst plan: automatic 50% burst via shared capacity or burst credits. Customer requested explicit throughput guarantees in contract (tokens/s and concurrency per-GPU).

SLA negotiation points: desired uptime 99.95%, p95 latency credit tiers (if missed >3 months in a quarter -> service credit), fallbacks: automatic failover to hosted model variant with 20% higher latency but lower cost. Legal asks clearer measurement language and dispute resolution clause referencing probe datasets.
Quote from VTC SRE: "If our p95 is higher than your SLA, we can't roll to prod — we need deterministic tails. We measure from user click to response render in mobile app."

Action items (short): agree on measurement spec; schedule 48h side-by-side; exchange probe scripts and test endpoints; provide formal dedicated capacity sizing + cost sheet; produce draft SLA wording for legal review.

Known risks: network egress variability at customer side; differences in client SDK buffering that alter observed first-byte times; potential need for edge placement to reach p50 targets in APAC users.

Internal SE opinion: set three SLO layers: observed-client (for product teams), server-gen (for Redwood ops), and contract-SLA (canonical probe harness). Keep contract tied to canonical probe harness measured from dedicated Redwood probe nodes in customer's VPC egress point to remove ambiguity.
Pricing sensitivity: VTC prefers fixed reserved monthly fee vs usage variable. Will push for blended model: committed GPUs + overage token pricing.
